## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 32* (entitled *Pattasaññī*) is an etiquette training rule (*sekhiya*) belonging to the Vinaya Piṭaka's *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*, governing mealtime deportment and instructing monastics to eat with their attention focused upon the almsbowl. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 It also shares close topical resemblances with rules regarding receiving alms with attention (*pattasaññīpaṭiggahaṇa*), notably *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 28* and corresponding rules in the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, and Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinayas.

DharmaNexus records no cross-language matches exceeding the score threshold of 10 [DharmaNexus].
